record.original_question: For each natural number n, is there a finite upper bound on the number of distinct geometric or combinatorial configurations that an n-cycle of Herman rings of period n can realize?

evidence.quote: Regarding possible configurations of Herman rings, we have the following question: Question: Is there any bound on the possible number of configurations of an n-cycle of Herman rings of period n in N?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let f be a transcendental meromorphic function on the complex plane having at least one omitted value (i.e., a value that is not in the image of f). A Herman ring of f is a periodic Fatou component U of period n, meaning f^n(U) = U with n minimal, such that f^n restricted to U is conformally conjugate to an irrational rotation of a round annulus. An n-cycle of Herman rings is an ordered family {U_0, U_1, …, U_{n-1}} of Herman rings with f(U_i) = U_{i+1 mod n} and minimal period n. Two n-cycles of Herman rings are said to have the same configuration if there is an orientation-preserving homeomorphism of the Riemann sphere carrying one cycle to the other while preserving the cyclic dynamical labeling and the nesting/separation pattern of the rings together with the locations of the poles and omitted values they surround.

Question: For each integer n ≥ 1, is there a finite upper bound C(n) on the number of distinct configurations that can be realized by an n-cycle of Herman rings of period n among all such meromorphic functions f with at least one omitted value?
artifact.status_search_result: The general question of whether the number of configurations of an n-cycle of Herman rings of period n is finite for every n is posed as an open question. Partial results are known for small periods: there is at most one configuration when the period is 3 or 4, and exactly six configurations are realized for period 5. No general bound for arbitrary n appears in the literature.

status_evidence.title: On periods of Herman rings and relevant poles
status_evidence.snippet: Lower bounds on the period p in terms of the number h of H-relevant poles: p ≥ h(h+1)/2 or p ≥ h(h+3)/2 depending on the situation.
status_evidence.claim: Period bounds in terms of relevant poles are known, but no general configuration count bound.

status_evidence.title: Two 5-cycles of Herman rings of configurations
status_evidence.snippet: Six configurations exist for 5-periodic Herman rings; for periods 3 or 4, at most one cycle of Herman rings.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results are known for small periods but the general question remains open.

status_evidence.title: Herman Rings: Structure, Dynamics, and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Question: Is there any bound on the possible number of configurations of an n-cycle of Herman rings of period n?
status_evidence.claim: The general configuration-count bound is listed as an open question.
